title: In Memory of W. B. Yeats

access.edition_or_version: Written February 1939; collected in Another Time, 1940

tone_mechanisms_observed: the ordinary world continuing indifferently while the poet dies (brooks, airports, statues)
three-part structure moving from impersonal winter scene to eulogy to aphoristic meditation
apostrophe and direct address to the dead poet, including ambivalent praise
the refusal of easy consolation: art is granted survival but not power
tenderness held together with ironic self-criticism
mechanics.emotional_progression: Cold impartial scene -> bodily dissolution and death -> public eulogy -> austere statement about art's survival without efficacy.
mechanics.point_of_view: Third-person report that shifts to direct address and then to generalizing reflection.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Varied line-lengths; clipped declaratives produce a wintry, withheld cadence.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Deliberate coolness in the opening increases tenderness by contrast; grief is delivered under restraint.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Modern elegy's melancholic turn (Ramazani): ambivalence, self-criticism, refusal of compensation. Verified as a documented modern elegy via Ramazani 1994 and Poetry Foundation.
mechanics.copyright_note: Copyrighted (Estate of W. H. Auden). Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
